explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/683: is there c > 0 with P(C(n,k)) ≥ min(n−k+1, k^{1+c}) for all 1 ≤ k ≤ n? The statement restricts to 0 < k ≤ n/2, which loses nothing. For k > n/2, write k' = n−k < k. Then min(n−k+1, k^{1+c}) ≤ k'+1, and P(C(n,k')) > k' by Sylvester–Schur, so the large-k range is automatic. P n k is the largest prime factor of C(n,k). Faithful.
